items.item: Covered Connecticut eligibility for a noncitizen at 100–138% of the poverty line who is barred from HUSKY D by immigration status
items.requirement: ENACTED: Covered Connecticut is for an adult 19–64 with household income to 175% of the poverty line who is "ineligible for HUSKY Health/Medicaid due to income", "eligible for financial help" (APTC and CSRs), using 100% of it, in a silver plan (portal.ct.gov/dss/health-and-home-care/covered-connecticut-program, read 2026-10-16); Access Health CT: "don't qualify for Medicaid due to income" and "If your household income makes you eligible for HUSKY Health/Medicaid, you are not eligible for the Covered CT Program" (help.accesshealthct.com/en_US/covered-connecticut-program, read 2026-10-16, 'Income Guidelines for 2026 Coverage'); the OHS eligibility summary of 8 July 2021 defined it as an income band above HUSKY's limit ("greater than 160%, and up to and including 175%" for parents). FEDERAL AUTHORITY: CMS's approval of 15 December 2022 (demonstration 11-W-00402/1, to 31 December 2027) authorizes expenditure for adults "who are not Medicaid eligible" to 175% and eligible for APTC, and describes them as having "income that is above the Medicaid limit" (medicaid.gov covered-ct-ca.pdf, read 2026-10-16). THE CREDIT: in 2026 a lawfully present noncitizen at 100–400% who is not eligible for other minimum essential coverage is an applicable taxpayer (26 USC 36B(c)(1)(A); 26 CFR 1.36B-2(b)(1)); the under-100% exception for the lawfully present barred by status (36B(c)(1)(B), 1.36B-2(b)(5)) was struck for taxable years after 2025 (Pub. L. 119-21 §71302); from 2027 only an "eligible alien" (green card, Cuban/Haitian entrant, COFA) has it (§71301; 45 CFR 155.305(f)(1)(ii)(C), 155.20, read 2026-10-16). UNCERTAINTY: no Access Health CT or DSS document read states how it treats a noncitizen barred from HUSKY D by status at 100–138%; the state's published words ("due to income"; "if your household income makes you eligible for HUSKY") are implemented, and the status-barred person is given the marketplace, whose credit the return gives from 100% (item 5).
items.currentBehavior: health.ts:430-431 (programFor): Covered Connecticut is given to anybody lawfully present whose last month is ≤175% of the year before's line and for whom creditAllowed (≥100% and creditStatus) holds; it never asks whether the income is over HUSKY D's 138%. A noncitizen barred from HUSKY D by status (medicaidStatus false from 1 October 2026, health.ts:330-334; 418 skipped) at 100–138% is given Covered Connecticut. Reproduced by reading: an F-1 student in 2026 with a month of $1,500.00 (between $1,304.17 and $1,835.40) falls through 418 to 431 and gets {kind:'essential'}. The return (taxreturn.ts:1033) also reads ≤138% as 'a person Medicaid would take' whatever the status, so the marketplace's credit is none for that person (and none at all for a 1040-NR filer, taxreturn.ts:1035; item 5).
items.plan: programFor: Covered Connecticut only where last month's income is over HUSKY D's line (current year, 138%) and within 175% of the year before's, whatever the status: an income HUSKY D's line takes is not 'ineligible due to income'. The status-barred person at 100–138% falls to the marketplace (open enrollment or 60 days), with the credit on the return from 100% (taxreturn: the 138% exclusion applies only where the status admits Medicaid). Dated comment with the sources and the uncertainty. Guide and Papers sentences updated.

items.item: Work-test exemptions (Pub. L. 119-21 §71119: mandatory and optional exceptions and the specified excluded individuals), applied before denial or termination where SLATE can read them
items.requirement: ENACTED: 42 USC 1396a(xx)(3) and (9)(A)(ii) (Pub. L. 119-21 §71119, govinfo PLAW-119publ21, read 2026-10-16); REGULATION: 42 CFR 435.551 (applicable individual: the adult group, 19 to under 65), 435.553 (mandatory exceptions: under 19, Medicare, mandatory groups, a specified excluded individual for part or all of the month, an inmate in the 3 months ending on the month's first day), 435.554 (specified excluded: former foster youth, Indians, parent/caretaker of a child 13 or under or a disabled individual, a 100% disabled veteran, the medically frail on the State's list, TANF compliance, "a member of a household that receives [SNAP] benefits ... and is not exempt from a work requirement under such Act", drug or alcohol treatment, inmates, pregnant/postpartum), 435.555 (optional short-term hardship: inpatient hospital or nursing facility care in the month, on the individual's request; a disaster or high-unemployment county; travel for care) — CMS-2454-IFC, published 3 June 2026, effective 31 July 2026 (public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-11094.pdf, read 2026-10-16). CONNECTICUT: "You do not have to meet the work rules if you: ... Are under 19 or over 64 years old; ... Were recently inpatient in a hospital or nursing facility; ... Are in a household receiving SNAP ... and not exempt from the SNAP work rules; Are medically frail and unable to work ..." (Connecticut Hospital Association, H.R. 1 HUSKY D Changes, Materials for Providers and Community-Based Organizations, adapted from DSS, dated 8/25/26, cthosp.org, read 2026-10-16).

items.item: Required notice and response periods: §71119's notice of noncompliance and 30 days to show compliance before denial or disenrollment; the advance notice at termination (42 CFR 431.211's 10 days); Connecticut's own. Order: notice, response window, then decision
items.requirement: ENACTED: 42 USC 1396a(xx)(6)(A): notice of noncompliance; "a period of 30 calendar days, beginning on the date on which such notice of noncompliance is received" to show compliance or an exception; an enrollee keeps medical assistance through it; then deny or disenroll "not later than the end of the month following the month in which such 30-calendar-day period ends", after considering every other basis and with written notice and a fair hearing. REGULATION: 42 CFR 435.558 (CMS-2454-IFC, read 2026-10-16): the notice names the months assessed, how to show compliance or an exception, the deadline, the consequences for Medicaid and for APTC/PTC, how to reapply, and the short-term hardship where elected; it "is considered to be received 5 days after the date on the notice" (c)(4); coverage continues until determined ineligible (a)(3); disenrollment after advance written notice (d)(2)(ii); no restriction on reapplying (e). 42 CFR 431.211: "at least 10 days before the date of action". CONNECTICUT: UPM 1570.10(A)(1): "the Department mails or gives adequate notice at least ten days prior to the date of the intended action if the Department intends to discontinue, terminate, suspend or reduce benefits", applied to a HUSKY D discontinuance by Access Health CT (DSS Notice of Decision, Request #740154, 2016, portal.ct.gov, read 2026-10-16). SLATE ASSUMPTION (CT's end-of-month practice not found): a cover found ineligible ends at the end of the month in which the ten days run out, which is never later than the statute's end of the month after the window.

items.item: The look-back at application and renewal: Connecticut's chosen period, applied at each
items.requirement: ENACTED: 1396a(xx)(1)(A): an applicant, "1 or more but not more than 3 (as specified by the State) consecutive months immediately preceding the month during which such individual applies"; (1)(B): an enrollee, "1 or more (as specified by the State) months, whether or not consecutive" between determinations, verified at the regularly scheduled redetermination. REGULATION: 42 CFR 435.556(a)-(b) (CMS-2454-IFC, read 2026-10-16). CONNECTICUT: "If not exempt from the work rules at initial application, eligibility includes a 1-month look back at work requirement compliance"; "At renewal, there will be a 6-month look back to verify the individual met work/community engagement requirements or was exempt from requirements during at least 1 calendar month" (CHA, H.R. 1 HUSKY D Changes, Materials For Providers, dated 8/25/26, adapted from DSS's, read 2026-10-16). UNCERTAINTY: no DSS page read states the periods directly; the CHA's materials are DSS's adapted. A FINDING ON THE WAY (its own item, 6): the monthly income criterion is MAGI-based household income, not wages alone.

items.item: Whether a nonresident-alien F-1 student qualifies for advance premium tax credits in 2026; what the engine should do in 2026 (the marketplace's credit, Covered Connecticut's dependence on it)
items.requirement: ENACTED (2026): an applicable taxpayer's household income at 100–400% (26 USC 36B(c)(1)(A)), filing jointly if married (36B(c)(1)(C)); a month of coverage counts only while lawfully present (36B(e)), which before §71301 took effect included nonimmigrant status (45 CFR 155.20 'lawfully present' (2): 'a valid nonimmigrant status, as defined in 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)'; an F-1 is 1101(a)(15)(F)). Nothing excludes a nonresident alien: 26 CFR 1.36B-2(b) has no such rule (law.cornell.edu, read 2026-10-16); IRS Pub. 974 (2025): "You must file Form 8962 with your income tax return (Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR)" when taking the PTC; Instructions for Form 1040-NR (2025): exceptions only for dependents, for the spouse's advance payments, and for a married 1040-NR filer (irs.gov, read 2026-10-16). The marketplace: 45 CFR 155.305(a)(1) and (f)(1) (read 2026-10-16). FROM 2027: only an 'eligible alien' (36B(e)(2)(B) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §71301, taxable years after 31 December 2026; 45 CFR 155.305(f)(1)(ii)(C)), which an F-1 student isn't. So in 2026 an unmarried F-1 student in status, not eligible for Yale Health or other minimum essential coverage, at 100–400%, qualifies for APTC and the PTC on Form 1040-NR; from 2027 she doesn't. SLATE's simulation: no advance payments are modeled; the whole premium is paid and the credit is taken on the return (health.ts header), and SLATE's lives are unmarried.

items.item: FOUND ON THE WAY: the work test's $580 a month is MAGI-based monthly income, not wages alone
items.requirement: REGULATION: 42 CFR 435.552(f): an applicable individual demonstrates community engagement for a month with "a monthly income that is not less than" the federal minimum wage × 80 ($580), and "(2) The agency must determine the monthly income based on the individual's MAGI-based income, for their MAGI-based household, as defined at § 435.603"; the preamble: "countable income under § 435.603(e) generally includes earned income as well as countable unearned income, meaning that States must take into account all of this income"; CMS "considered counting only earned income" and rejected it (CMS-2454-IFC, read 2026-10-16). CT: "Monthly income of at least $580/month" (CHA 8/25/26).
